connector: While the children were finding Aslan, Caspian was losing hope in the dark of Aslan’s How. Tonight Nikabrik brings two strange guests to the council. You have a pattern now, and a word for it. Today, turn it into a sentence about what the book believes.

a.raw: nikabrik wanted caspian dead but trufflehunter the badger said we dont change we hold on
a.fixed: Nikabrik wanted Caspian dead, but Trufflehunter the badger said, “We don’t change. We hold on.”
a.why: Capitals on the three names; a comma before but; a comma before the quotation; don’t needs an apostrophe; Trufflehunter’s words from Chapter 5 are two short sentences inside the quotation marks.

b.raw: caspian said i am sorry for nikabrik
b.why: Capitals on Caspian, I and Nikabrik; a comma before the quotation; the period goes inside the closing quotation mark.

notes.wgrd: Turn the pattern into a theme sentence: what repeats, what happens to people who choose each way, then cut the names so it is true about people.
vocab: A very steep cliff or drop.
A rough camp without proper shelter.
Able to feel and sense things; aware.
Betraying your own king or country.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: rupt = break, duct and duce = lead, form = shape: interrupt, conduct, introduce, transform.
notes.grammar: Commas in dates and places: a comma between the day and the year (June 12, 1941), between a town and its county or country (Dover, Kent), and another after them if the sentence goes on. Narnia has no calendar, so practice dates are made up.
notes.spelling: Greek and Latin parts you know: port (carry), spect (look), script and scribe (write), rupt (break), tele (far). Spell the part the same way every time: inter + rupt + ion.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: In Chapter 12, Caspian’s council faces a terrible offer. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Nikabrik says the Dwarfs are always sent on the dangerous raids and go short when the rations fail. The Badger answers, “Lies! All lies!”
items.why: He says out loud that something is false, to an angry Dwarf with a weapon.
items.hint: Is it safe to say this?

items.t: Peter meets Caspian for the first time and says, “I haven’t come to take your place, you know, but to put you into it.”
items.why: The High King uses his power to help Caspian, not to replace him.
items.hint: Who could Peter have made king?

items.t: Peter thanks Trufflehunter for never doubting them. The Badger says, “No credit to me, your Majesty. I’m a beast and we don’t change.”
items.why: He held on to the truth for a very long time.
items.hint: What does holding on mean here?

items.t: Caspian says, “I am sorry for Nikabrik, though he hated me from the first moment he saw me.”
items.why: He is fair even to someone who wanted him dead.
items.hint: How does Caspian speak of his enemy?

transcripts.welcome: Hello, it’s Nell. While the children found Aslan, Caspian’s side was losing hope in the dark. Today’s question: when people have to choose whom to trust, what does this book seem to believe?
transcripts.read: This is a dark chapter. Watch Nikabrik’s road and Peter’s road side by side. Where does each one lead? Then, at the end, listen to what Caspian says about Nikabrik. It tells you a lot about Caspian.
transcripts.spelling: Long words are built from parts you already know. Find the part, and spell it the same way every time. Portable: port, able. Spectator: spect, a, tor. The part never changes its spelling, even when the word around it does.

steps: Read the tip and the lenses.
Tap the lens you will use today.
Keep it in mind as you read. Your note boxes are on the Reading tab.
Tap each yellow part of the first sentence to see why it is correct.
Pick Sentence A or Sentence B.
Type it the right way in the box, then tap Check My Work.
Read the sentence and the note under it.
Copy it in cursive in your reading journal, slowly.
Look at each root and its choices.
Tap every part that makes a real word.
Tap Show Answers to check.
Read the word meanings.
Type the word that fits each sentence.
Tap Check My Answers.
Read the worked example.
Punctuate the practice sentence.
Write it a second way with the date at the end, and say which you’d keep.
Read the Before and After.
Type the meaning of each root in one word.
Tap Check My Work.
In the box, build and break apart three words.
Read the two Pause & Think questions first.
Keep them in mind as you read.
Open your book and read Chapter 12.
Fill in the note boxes as you read.
After you read, do the Seven Pillars Watch at the end of this tab.
Read Trufflehunter’s words.
Think through Reader and Writer.
Write your own two sentences with the same pattern.
Pick Explorer or Scholar.
Answer all three questions in full sentences.
Use a detail from the book in every answer. The hint under each question helps.
Last, write one or two sentences about your reading lens.
